excerpts.title: Mesh density and field resolution
excerpts.summary: A finer FEM mesh resolves sharper gradients near supports, corners, braces, and load patches. A coarse mesh can smooth out stress concentrations even when the boundary conditions are correct.
excerpts.watch: Compare where deformation is largest against where von Mises stress peaks. If the stress hot spot moves or sharpens after refinement, the previous mesh was under-resolving the field.
excerpts.try: Increase structured cells per side and rerun the solve before using the FEM field as the PINN comparison baseline.

excerpts.title: Collocation points
excerpts.summary: PINNs do not see a mesh in the FEM sense. They enforce the PDE at sampled interior collocation points and enforce supports or loading at boundary points.
excerpts.watch: Sparse interior points can leave the displacement field patchy. Sparse boundary points can make supports and traction loading unreliable.
excerpts.try: Adjust both domain and boundary point counts before the first baseline run so the student sees how each point family affects the learning problem.

excerpts.title: PDE loss versus boundary loss
excerpts.summary: PDE loss measures interior equilibrium, while boundary-condition loss measures whether supports and traction are enforced. Either term can dominate training and hide the other failure mode.
excerpts.watch: If boundary loss is much larger than PDE loss, the model is usually struggling with supports or loading. If PDE loss dominates, equilibrium inside the domain is the bottleneck.
excerpts.try: Change only one loss weight at a time, rerun, and compare whether the stress field or boundary behavior improves.

excerpts.title: Why Neumann loading is hard
excerpts.summary: A traction boundary condition constrains derivatives of the displacement field, not displacement values directly. That makes localized load patches harder for a PINN than fixed displacement constraints. If teacher points are added on the load patch, those teacher points are still direct displacement anchors; they do not become Neumann supervision.
excerpts.watch: The most visible mismatch often appears near the top load patch, where peak stress is localized and derivative-sensitive. But if load-patch teacher points still underperform, the usual issue is not that they are indirect; it is that patch-only guidance is too localized to stabilize the whole field.
excerpts.try: Use the FEM comparison tab to identify whether the error is mostly local to the patch or spread through the frame before choosing between boundary, interior, or mixed teacher-point settings.

excerpts.title: Teacher-guided supervision
excerpts.summary: Teacher points add sparse FEM displacement targets on top of the physics losses. They are direct displacement supervision regardless of where they are placed, but the best placement should be tested rather than assumed.
excerpts.watch: Boundary or interior teacher points can stabilize the global displacement and stress field. Load-patch teacher points may still help locally, but patch-only guidance can be too concentrated to reduce whole-field error as effectively.
excerpts.try: Compare a boundary-only or interior-only teacher run against the baseline before escalating to mixed or load-patch guidance.

excerpts.title: Adaptive sampling and Fourier features
excerpts.summary: Residual-adaptive sampling moves attention toward high-error regions, while Fourier features help the network represent sharper spatial variation. Both can help when stress is too smooth near localized features.
excerpts.watch: Adaptive sampling should concentrate points around difficult regions. Fourier sigma that is too high can make training noisy; too low may still look overly smooth.
excerpts.try: Try adaptive sampling first for residual localization, then enable Fourier features with a modest sigma when the stress field remains too smooth.

excerpts.title: Normalization and network capacity
excerpts.summary: Input normalization stabilizes optimization by keeping coordinates on a friendly numerical scale. Network width and depth control representational capacity, but more capacity is not automatically better if losses are poorly balanced.
excerpts.watch: If losses are noisy or fail to decrease, normalization and learning stability matter before adding layers. If the field is consistently too smooth after stable training, capacity may be too low.
excerpts.try: Keep normalization on for the teaching workflow and change architecture only after the baseline loss behavior is understandable.
